rows.item: Actual Hayabusa re-entry capsule (returned Itokawa samples 13 June 2010)
rows.notes: Permanent exhibit since 11 July 2023, Global Gallery 2F, Japan's Space Development. Only the capsule flew back; the orbiter itself burned up. Sagamihara City Museum showed the capsule in 2010/2021 (temporary, not confirmed current).

rows.item: Actual Hayabusa2 re-entry capsule (returned Ryugu samples Dec 2020)
rows.notes: Exhibited since June 2023 in the Communication Hall of Space Science and Exploration; a secondary search summary called it permanent but the fetched ISAS page only says the display began June 2023. Only the capsule, not the orbiter, is on display.

rows.item: Pioneer H flight spare hung in Boeing Milestones of Flight Hall as stand-in for Pioneer 10
rows.notes: Wikipedia (quoting Van Allen) says it is a flight-worthy spare built from Pioneer F/G spares, but the NASM collection page (A19770451000) calls it a TRW-built prototype/replica. Conflicting; operator to decide.

rows.item: Pioneer H flight spare hung in Boeing Milestones of Flight Hall (stands in for Pioneer 10/11)
rows.notes: Same unit as for pioneer-10; same conflict between Wikipedia (real spare) and NASM catalogue (prototype/replica).

rows.item: Vega Solar System Probe Bus and Landing Apparatus engineering model
rows.notes: NASM page says the Vega engineering model is on display at Udvar-Hazy; catalogue calls it an engineering model refurbished for display in 1992 (NASM-2005-29880). Not clear whether it is flight-standard hardware or a display model. Applies to the Vega class (also vega-2).

rows.item: Vega Solar System Probe Bus and Landing Apparatus engineering model
rows.notes: Same unit as for vega-1; see notes there.

Evidence page returned HTTP 403 to me; claim rests on search-result summaries (SpaceNews and NRL) that the engineering model was transferred to NASM and is on view at Udvar-Hazy awaiting conservation. Not verified by reading the page.
